story.originalTitle: How Carlos Sainz bounced back from the most difficult moment of his F1 career
story.summaryEn: Carlos Sainz spoke to Motorsport.com on the eve of the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, recalling his first podium with Williams in Baku a year earlier while acknowledging that the FW48 has not allowed him to achieve the results he hoped for in recent months.
detailZh: 塞恩斯如何从F1生涯最艰难的时刻重回正轨
威廉姆斯车手在阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末开始时接受了Motorsport.com的采访
对塞恩斯来说，巴库永远不会只是一个普通的比赛地。上周在2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛前夕接受我们采访时，这位西班牙车手刚刚抵达这座城市，思绪不可避免地回到了12个月前——当时他在威廉姆斯首次登上领奖台。
这仍然是他认为自己职业生涯最佳时刻之一，但2026年的塞恩斯是在经历了几个月的困难之后来到巴库的，在此期间FW48赛车未能让他取得期望的成绩。
然而，从个人的角度来看，他的感受几乎完全相反：32岁的他觉得自己正处于职业生涯的巅峰附近，驾驶水平非常高。正是这种反差——他在方向盘后的自我感觉与成绩上的匮乏之间的矛盾——让这段时期格外令人沮丧。
MS：卡洛斯，你好吗？
卡洛斯·塞恩斯：“我很好。我昨天抵达这里准备比赛周末。这个地方让我回忆起去年的许多美好时光，那是我与威廉姆斯车队的第一个领奖台。那可能是我职业生涯中最美好的时刻之一，所以巴库现在对我而言是一个重要的地方。”
现在这个时刻，在你的生活和职业生涯中是怎样的一个时刻？
“这是一个特殊的时刻，因为就我个人的表现而言，我觉得自己度过了不错的一年。我今年32岁，我认为自己正处于职业生涯的巅峰附近。我感觉自己今年开得相当不错，但与此同时，这个赛季一直非常令人沮丧，赛车出现了很多问题，使我们无法取得好成绩。
“在某种程度上，我觉得这正在变成我职业生涯中有点荒废的一年，因为我们没能达到我们为自己设定的目标。我希望这只是一个奇怪的年份，希望下个赛季我们能发现自己处于更好的位置。”
你于2025年加入威廉姆斯，但在那之前你曾效力于小红牛、雷诺、迈凯伦和法拉利。你认为你为这支车队带来了什么？自从你来到这里之后，威廉姆斯发生了多大的变化？
“首先，我带来了我的经验以及作为一名车手速度。在一级方程式度过12年之后，我想差不多每个人都知道我的优势是什么。但最重要的是，我认为我带来了经验和一种特定的工作方式，努力帮助这支车队进步。
“我有机会体验过像法拉利这样的顶级车队，所以我可以给威廉姆斯一个参照，让他们知道一支顶级车队如今是什么水平，以及要达到那个水平还需要什么。
“好的一面是，我们还有詹姆斯·沃尔斯，他来自梅赛德斯，还有亚历克斯（阿尔本），他经历过红牛的环境。车队内部有三四个重要人物，他们都知道一支顶级车队是如何运作的。我们正在努力让威廉姆斯在未来回到那个水平。”
你已经决定把自己的未来托付给威廉姆斯。除了技术层面的原因之外，你在这支车队的成员身上看到了什么，让你愿意继续相信这个项目？
“主要有两个原因。第一是我信任这个项目、这些人以及车队的中长期愿景。诚然，今年非常令人失望，是一个谁都没有预料到的赛季。它也让我们看到我们还有多少需要改进的地方，而且我们距离目标可能比我们想象的还要远。
“去年情况几乎相反：我们取得了比预期还要好的成绩。而今年则困难得多。第二个原因是，从我到达的第一刻起就感到宾至如归。在威廉姆斯，我感觉到人们真正在倾听我，对于一名车手来说这是最根本的。我希望当我说的时候，人们会听，而且某些事情能够朝我建议的方向推进。
“到目前为止，这里正是这样。我职业生涯中最好的几个年头是在迈凯伦度过的，在法拉利的一些岁月也是如此。比如在迈凯伦，我当时的感受与现在在威廉姆斯的感受非常相似。我认为，当车手身处那样的环境时，才能发挥出最佳水平。”
你常常把自己形容为一个非常理性的人。但是否也有一个卡洛斯·塞恩斯，很难把赛道上的糟糕一天抛在脑后？
“当然有。当某一天事情不顺利时，我是那个上床睡觉时还会为所犯的错误而痛苦的人。但经验给了我很重要的一点：明白世界并不会就此终结。我们都有过好的周末和坏的周末。生活继续向前，一名车手的价值不会因为一场糟糕的比赛就突然下降。
“随着经验的积累，你学会如何在心理上应对这些情况。你知道那只是一场比赛，也许下一站在巴库你就登上领奖台，所有人都会忘记之前发生的事，突然之间你又被看作一个不同的车手。在这方面，经验的作用非常大。”
你职业生涯中最艰难的时刻是什么？
“毫无疑问是在得知我将离开法拉利之后的那几个月。说实话，我以为自己会在那里待很长时间。我们一起度过了美好的四年，我认为夏尔（勒克莱尔）和我合作得很好，车队也在朝着正确的方向前进。
“我从未想过会离开法拉利，但那种情况还是发生了，我需要两三个月的时间重新找回自己，弄清楚我想如何继续自己的职业生涯，以及我的下一个目标是什么。
“那几个月很艰难，但我想正是因为那段艰难，我后来才找到了职业生涯的最佳状态。我在澳大利亚赢了，登上了领奖台，我觉得我的2024赛季非常强劲。”
那么最好的时刻是什么呢？
“我在迈凯伦的岁月里有很多美好的回忆。我非常享受为那支车队效力，并在那里第一次登上领奖台。
“然后还有在法拉利的那些胜利。很难形容车手赢得职业生涯头几场比赛时的感受。而且我认为那四场胜利到来的方式，让每一场都变得特别。
“然后就是和威廉姆斯车队一起登上领奖台的经历。我当初选择这支车队是一次冒险，也许有些人觉得我疯了。后来我们在赛季末段拿下了三次领奖台，一切似乎都在朝着完美的方向发展。
“这正是为什么今年的情况让人难以理解。这是一个非常复杂的赛季。
你在赛车运动中背负着一个非常重要的姓氏。有没有那么一段时间，身为塞恩斯家族的一员更像是一种负担而不是一种荣耀？
“是的，尤其是在我参加卡丁车赛的最初几年。那时候，我感觉这个姓氏带给我的压力要大于它能带来的好处。小时候，我深切地感受到这种压力。我能看到，也能感觉到，因为我父亲的缘故，别人对待我的方式不一样。
“有过一些非常艰难的情况，我现在不想谈论，但在11岁到14岁之间，我还在跑卡丁车的时候，经历过一些糟糕的时刻。也许有一天我会在一本自传里谈到它们。我确实感受到了压力，我也看到有些人对一个十二三岁的男孩表现得很恶劣。我不喜欢那样。”
如果今天你能见到15岁或16岁的塞恩斯，你会告诉他这一切都是值得的吗？在“普通”青少年的生活中，有没有什么经历是你觉得自己错过的？
“我肯定会告诉他，这一切都是值得的。我从来没有真正有过一刻去质疑自己所做的一切是否值得这些牺牲，因为我一直都很享受。
“驾驶、去参赛、去竞争——这始终是我的梦想。即使我错过了16岁的孩子可能会拥有的某些普通经历，我也从不把它看作一种牺牲。我只是觉得，我正在做自己想做的事。
“当然，也有过紧张和压力的时刻，也有过我不知道自己能否进入F1、能否真正成为一名F1车手的时刻。
“对于那个曾经怀疑自己能否有朝一日达到这个高度、甚至能否在F1中赢得分站赛的男孩，我会告诉他不要担心。他会成功的。而且他的职业生涯可能会比他想象的还要好。”
detailEn: How Carlos Sainz bounced back from the most difficult moment of his F1 career
The Williams driver spoke to Motorsport.com at the start of the Azerbaijan GP weekend

Baku can never be just another place for Carlos Sainz. When we spoke to him on the eve of the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix last week, the Spaniard had only just arrived in the city and his thoughts inevitably went back to 12 months ago, having claimed his first podium with Williams.

It remains one of the moments he still considers among the best of his career, but in 2026 Sainz arrived in Baku after a difficult few months, during which the FW48 has not allowed him to achieve the results he had hoped for.

And yet, from a personal point of view, his perception is almost the opposite: at 32, he feels he is close to the peak of his career and driving at a very high level. It is precisely this contrast, between how he feels behind the wheel and the lack of results, that has made this period particularly frustrating.
MS: Carlos, how are you?

Carlos Sainz: “I’m good. I arrived yesterday for the race weekend. It’s a place that brings back a lot of great memories from last year, from my first podium with Williams. It was probably one of the best moments of my career, so Baku is now an important place for me.”
What kind of moment is this in your life and in your career?

“It’s a particular moment because, in terms of my own performance, I feel like I’m having a good year. I’m 32 and I think I’m close to the peak of my career. I feel like I’m driving quite well this year, but at the same time it has been a very frustrating season, with a lot of problems with the car that have prevented us from achieving good results.

“In a way, I feel like it is becoming a bit of a lost year in my career because we are not managing to reach the targets we had set ourselves. I hope it can simply be a strange year and that next season we can find ourselves in a better position.”

You joined Williams in 2025, but before that you raced for Toro Rosso, Renault, McLaren and Ferrari. What do you think you have brought to this team, and how much has Williams changed since you arrived?

“First of all, I brought my experience and my speed as a driver. After 12 years in Formula 1, I think more or less everyone knows what my strengths are. But above all, I think I have brought experience and a certain way of working, trying to help this team improve.
“I have had the chance to experience top teams such as Ferrari, so I can give Williams a reference for where a top team is today and what is needed to reach that level.

“The positive thing is that we also have James Vowles, who comes from Mercedes, and Alex [Albon], who has experienced the Red Bull environment. There are three or four important figures within the team who know how a top team works. We are trying to bring Williams back to that level in the future.”
You have decided to commit your future to Williams. Beyond the technical reasons, what have you seen in the people within this team that convinced you to keep believing in the project?

“There are two main reasons. The first is that I trust the project, the people and the medium- to long-term vision within the team. It is true that this year has been very disappointing, a season nobody expected. It has also shown us how much we still need to improve and that we are probably further away than we thought.

“Last year it was almost the opposite: we achieved results that were even better than expected. This year, instead, has been much more difficult. The second reason is that I have felt at home from the very first moment I arrived. At Williams, I have felt that people really listen to me, and for me as a driver that is fundamental. I want to feel that when I speak, people listen and that certain things can move in the direction I suggest.

“So far, that is exactly what has happened here. Some of the best years of my career were at McLaren, and also some of my years at Ferrari. At McLaren, for example, I felt in a very similar way to how I feel now at Williams. And I think a driver is able to perform at his best when he finds himself in that kind of environment.”
You have often described yourself as a very rational person. But is there also a Carlos Sainz who struggles to leave a bad day at the track behind him?

“Definitely. I’m the first one who, when I go to bed after a day in which things have not gone well, suffers thinking about the mistakes that were made. But experience has given me something very important: the understanding that the world does not end there. We have all had good weekends and bad weekends. Life goes on, and a driver’s value does not suddenly decrease because of one bad race.

“With experience, you learn how to manage those situations mentally. You know it is only one race, and maybe at the next one you finish on the podium in Baku, everyone forgets what happened before and suddenly you are seen as a different driver. Experience helps massively in that respect.”
What has been the most difficult moment of your career?

“Definitely the months after finding out that I would be leaving Ferrari. Honestly, I thought I was going to stay there for a long time. We had come through four good years in which I think Charles [Leclerc] and I had done a good job together, and the team was moving in the right direction.

“I never expected to leave Ferrari, but that situation happened and I needed two or three months to find myself again, understand how I wanted to continue my career and what my next objective would be.

“They were difficult months, but I think it was precisely because of that difficulty that I probably found the best form of my career afterwards. I won in Australia, achieved podiums and I think I had a very strong 2024 season.”
And what has been the best moment?
“I have so many great memories from my years at McLaren. I really enjoyed driving for that team and achieving my first podiums there.

"Then there were the wins with Ferrari. It is impossible to describe what a driver feels when he wins the first races of his career. And I think the way those four victories came makes every one of them special.

“Then there was the podium with Williams. I had taken my gamble by choosing this team and maybe some people thought I was crazy. Then we achieved three podiums towards the end of the season and everything seemed to be moving in the perfect direction.
“That is exactly why this year has been difficult to understand. It has been a really complicated season.”
You carry a very important surname in motorsport. Was there ever a time when being a Sainz felt more like a burden than a privilege?

“Yes, definitely during my first years in karting. At that time, I felt that the weight of my surname was greater than the advantages it could bring me. When I was young, I felt that pressure a lot. I could see it and I could feel that I was not being treated in the same way because of who my father was.

“There were some very difficult situations that I don’t want to talk about now, but between the ages of 11 and 14, while I was karting, I went through some bad moments. Maybe one day I will talk about them in a biography. I definitely felt the pressure, and I saw some people behave badly towards a 12- or 13-year-old boy. I did not like that.”
If you could meet the 15- or 16-year-old Carlos today, would you tell him it was all worth it? Is there anything from the life of a ‘normal’ teenager that you feel you missed out on?
“I would definitely tell him that it was worth it. I never really had a moment in which I questioned whether everything I was doing was worth the sacrifice, because I always enjoyed it.

“Driving, going to races, competing — it was always my dream. Even when I missed out on some of the normal experiences a 16-year-old might have, I never saw it as a sacrifice. I simply thought I was doing what I wanted to do.
“Of course, there were moments of tension and pressure, moments when I didn’t know whether I would make it to Formula 1 or whether I would really become a Formula 1 driver.

“To that boy who had doubts about whether he would one day make it here, or even win races in Formula 1, I would tell him not to worry. He will make it. And he will probably have an even better career than he ever imagined.”

detailZh: 博塔斯解释他在阿塞拜疆F1的糟糕表现
减震器“性能衰减”问题和旧规格法拉利动力单元造成了较大的性能差距
博塔斯为他阿塞拜疆大奖赛不佳的表现提出了自己的看法，认为减震器性能衰减让他的凯迪拉克在比赛过程中的行驶特性越来越差。
这位芬兰车手在巴库的整个周末都举步维艰，基本牢牢占据成绩榜末位。而队友塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在这座阿塞拜疆首都的赛道上延续了一贯的强势周末，这条赛道历来是这位墨西哥车手的福地。
博塔斯的比赛在最后一圈结束，他在15号弯撞上护栏，撞车时赛车的动力单元未能在超级压弯（superclipping）过程中为后轴提供正确的发动机制动力。
回顾阿塞拜疆大奖赛，博塔斯承认这是一个“相当糟糕”的周末，并解释了导致他表现平淡的几个关键问题。
“我明白从外面看起来相当糟糕；我在车里也感觉很糟。根本没办法跟上大部队，”博塔斯说道。
“比赛中我尝试了一切。得到了很多关于我在哪里损失时间的反馈。很大一部分是在直道上。但也有相当大一块是在整圈的各个弯角里都有损失。所以我就一直坚持推进到最后。这也是为什么我在最后一圈的1号弯出现了锁死。”
"最主要的是，我们在练习赛中就已经看到我的速度不足。我无法像佩雷斯那样在弯道中保持同样的速度。所以我们为排位赛做了很多改动，包括一些减震器和底板。实际上感觉好多了。"
"但在比赛中，行驶表现又退化得很厉害。我认为这和减震器有关，[它们]会随着温度升高而退化。"
"底板[也一样]，我们在这里那里还缺少一些压力测量点。所以我们[还]没有掌握空气动力学部件的完整信息，不像我过去习惯的那样，可以立刻看出自己是快了还是慢了。"
"但现在底板有些部分我们是盲区。不过对我来说，从感觉上讲，更多是行驶表现的问题，再加上动力转向在整个周末[不断退化]，导致我在比赛中也很难感受到赛车状态。所以，这些因素叠加在一起。"
博塔斯解释了为什么相比佩雷斯存在性能差距——他在直道上始终慢6到7公里每小时，原因在于队友换上了新的法拉利动力单元；佩雷斯用的是法拉利“ADUO 2”发动机，而博塔斯用的还是旧规格的动力单元。
在谈到凯迪拉克与其他车队整体差距时，博塔斯认为这支美国车队的基础设施相当扎实并且还在不断改进，但他解释说，为了赶工设计和制造他们的第一辆一级方程式赛车而进行的“仓促推进”，导致最终性能做出了妥协。
这与新车队负责人马尔钦·布德科夫斯基的说法相符，他指出车队为了赶上生产期限不得不走一些捷径。
“在调校方面，比如差速器映射、刹车映射等等，我们处于一个不错的状态，”博塔斯解释道。“我觉得我需要的东西都有。在发动机刹车映射这些方面，法拉利的支持也很到位。我们目前的主要限制仍然是在机械层面。”
"显然，设计这辆赛车的时间有点仓促。我们有一些不错的工具，但还没有达到我们希望的先进程度。而且明年的赛车在悬挂方面肯定会有改动，这将为调校方面的变化打开更多机会。但这正是我们欠缺的地方，也就是机械方面。"
谈到自己在巴库的比赛周末，佩雷斯认为"我在方向盘后面做出了巨大的差别"，在那场比赛中，这位前红牛车手一度看起来有望爆冷拿到一个积分。
比赛重启后，佩雷斯一度处于前十名的边缘，但最终掉了下去，因为他无法跟上身前的赛车。即使换了法拉利的新引擎，他也表示超车模式仍不足以抵消凯迪拉克MAC-26的阻力输出。
他表示，本周末在马来西亚雪邦赛道举行的巴林大奖赛上，车队将照常运作，不能再依靠他对巴库的特殊感情了。
"我认为目前的问题基本上是缺乏下压力，我们的赛车严重缺乏下压力，而且阻力也不大," 他说。"你知道，在巴库，我基本上整场比赛都保持在超车模式上，因此我能够跟上其他车手，但当我超越他们之后，我就完全是个乘客了，因为我没有直道速度。
"所以我们有两个大问题：没有下压力而且阻力很大——但我们一直都清楚，第一年会很艰难。
"很多事都可能发生，但我想，鉴于目前赛车的速度水平，我们差距太大了，而且这是一个很容易超车的地方。
"我对这个周末的前景并不太兴奋。我认为巴库只是个例外；在那里我做出了巨大的差异，而在这里，就赛车目前的状态而言，一切将回归我们的现实。
减震器的“衰减”会如何损害悬挂系统？
简单来说，当车轮压上路肩或颠簸而抬升时，或者当赛车承受任何形式的轴向运动时，减震器帮助控制通过扭力杆传递的能量。
在整场比赛过程中，减震器内部液体的压缩会产生热量。随着持续压缩，热量会改变液体的特性并降低其粘度，这意味着减震器产生的阻尼会变小。
因此，悬挂系统整体无法再吸收来自颠簸和路肩冲击的那么多能量，这意味着这些作用力会转而通过车架传递。
对于像巴库这样颠簸的赛道，燃油载荷开始对赛车的操控性能产生影响。底板表现也会出现小幅变化，因为这会对赛车的离地高度产生轻微影响。
detailEn: Valtteri Bottas reveals causes of his Azerbaijan F1 horror show
Damper "degradation" issue and the old-spec Ferrari power unit created a large performance deficit

Valtteri Bottas has offered theories behind his off-colour Azerbaijan Grand Prix performance, suggesting that damper degradation was giving his Cadillac increasingly poor ride characteristics through the race.

The Finn endured a struggle through the weekend at Baku, largely cemented to the bottom of the timesheets. This was magnified by team-mate Sergio Perez enjoying a characteristically strong weekend around the Azerbaijani capital, a circuit at which the Mexican has historically shone.
Bottas' race ended on the final lap with a crash into the barrier at Turn 15, in which the car's power unit failed to offer the correct level of engine braking on the rear axle while superclipping.
Reflecting on the Azerbaijan GP, Bottas admitted that it was a "pretty poor" weekend and explained some of the key problems that led to his muted showing.
"I understand it looked pretty bad from the outside; I felt pretty bad in the car as well. There was just no way to keep up with the pack," Bottas reckoned.

"Tried everything during the race. Got lots of feedback on where I am losing the time. A lot of it was on the straights. But also a big chunk was just all around the lap in the corners. That's why I just kept pushing until the end. And that's why I had the lock-up on the last lap in Turn 1.

"The main thing was we saw already in practice that I was lacking pace. I couldn't carry the same speed through the corners as Checo. So we changed a lot for the qualifying, including some dampers, the floor. And it actually felt a lot better.
"But then the ride again during the race degraded quite a lot. I think it's something to do with dampers, [degrading] with heat.

"The floor [too], we are still lacking a bit of pressure tappings here and there. So we don't [yet] have the full information on aero parts that I'm used to from the past where you could immediately see if you're down or up.

"But now there are some bits of the floor where we are blind. But for me, feeling-wise, it was more the ride, and that's in combination with power steering that was [degrading] throughout the weekend, and I was really then also struggling to feel the car throughout the race. So, those things combined."

Bottas explained the performance deficit to Perez, where he was consistently 6-7km/h slower on the straights, was down to the impact of his team-mate's new Ferrari powertrain; Perez had Ferrari's "ADUO 2" engine, while Bottas had the old-spec power unit.

Speaking about Cadillac's wider deficit to the other teams, Bottas reckoned that the American squad's infrastructure was pretty strong and continuing to improve, but explained that the "rush" to get its first F1 car designed and built had led to its ultimate performance being compromised.
This tallies with comments from new team principal Marcin Budkowski, who noted that the team had needed to make shortcuts to meet its production deadlines.

"When it comes to settings, like differential maps, brake maps and stuff, we're in a good place," Bottas explained. "I feel like I've got everything that I need. Also the support from Ferrari when it comes to the engine braking maps and stuff. The main limitation we have is still mechanically.

"Obviously it was a bit of a rush to design the car. We have some good tools, but not as advanced as we would hope. And there's going to be, for sure, a change to the suspension on next year's car. So that will open more opportunities for set-up changes. But that's where we're lacking, the mechanical side."

Speaking about his own Baku weekend, Perez reckoned that "I was making a massive difference" behind the wheel, in a race where the ex-Red Bull driver – briefly – looked like an outside bet for a surprise point.

Perez was on the cusp of the top 10 after the restart, but ended up falling back as he was unable to stay in touch with the cars ahead. Even with Ferrari's new engine, he stated that the overtake mode was not enough to counter the Cadillac MAC-26's drag output.
He suggested that it would be business as usual for the team at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix at Malaysia's Sepang circuit, without his affinity for Baku to fall back on.

"I think at the moment it's basically the lack of load, we have a massive lack of load in the car, and not a lot of drag," he said. "You know, in Baku, when I basically stayed on the overtake mode for the entire race and therefore I was able to stay with the others, but when I overtook them, I was just a passenger because I had no straightline speed.
"So we have two big issues: no load and a lot of drag – but we always knew this first year was going to be tricky.
"A lot can happen but, I guess given where the pace of the car is at the moment, we are just too far off and it's a place that you can overtake easily.

"I'm not too excited about the prospects for this weekend. I think Baku was a one-off; I was making a massive difference there, and here it will be just back to our reality in terms of where the car is at the moment."
How does damper 'degradation' hurt the suspension?
In short, the damper helps to control the energy moving through the torsion bars when the wheel jacks up over a kerb or a bump, or when the car sustains any kind of axial motion.

Through the course of a race, the compression of the fluid within the damper creates heat. With continued compression, the heat changes the properties of the fluid and the viscosity reduces, meaning that the damper produces less resistance.
As such, the suspension package overall can't absorb as much energy from bumps and kerb strikes, meaning that the forces are thus redirected through the chassis.
For a bumpy circuit like Baku, it can start to impact the handling of the car. There is also a small shift in floor performance, as this can produce a small impact on the ride height of the car.
keyPointsZh: 减震器性能衰减是博塔斯对赛车行驶特性变差的主要怀疑原因。

队友佩雷斯在巴库这条他历来擅长的赛道上表现强势，进一步放大了博塔斯的困境。
keyPointsEn: Damper degradation is Bottas's main suspicion for his car's worsening ride characteristics.

detailZh: 丰田否认2027年与奥孔达成WEC协议
这家日本制造商不想破坏其车手阵容内部的和谐
奥孔在F1的选择正逐渐减少，而丰田不会在世界耐力锦标赛（WEC）为他提供席位。
在哈斯车队本周官宣将在2026赛季结束后结束与这位30岁法国车手的合作之后，媒体上关于奥孔职业生涯下一步去向的猜测甚嚣尘上。
随着阿斯顿·马丁确认将继续留用阿隆索和斯特罗尔，凯迪拉克实际上成为奥孔在一级方程式中最后一个现实的选择。
这也正是他还与转投世界耐力锦标赛的可能性联系在一起的原因——可能加盟丰田。但丰田顾问亚历山大·伍尔茨现已向Motorsport.com姊妹刊物Formel1.de的YouTube频道明确表示：“这些传闻毫无根据。”
伍尔茨表示，丰田在勒芒及其世界耐力锦标赛项目上通常会做“相当长远的”规划，目前不打算对现有的六人车手阵容做出任何调整。
“因为当你把三个强势个性放进同一辆赛车时，他们需要时间去彼此接受，去找到正确的调校和正确的合作方式，并达到这样一个阶段：他们不再在内部互相竞争，而是真正激发出彼此的最佳状态。这是一个非常重要的区别，”这位奥地利人解释道。
#8 丰田Gazoo Racing 丰田TR010：塞巴斯蒂安·布耶米、布伦登·哈特利、平川亮
"这是丰田的优势之一：我们拥有这样的车队架构和车队文化，而这种东西不可能一夜之间改变。
"首先，我们签的是长期合同。其次，你不可能随便从外面引进一名车手，直接把他塞进车手阵容里。那样做恰恰有可能破坏我们自2012年以来一直建立并悉心呵护的文化。维护这种文化是我作为顾问、作为与车手密切合作的人的主要职责之一。
他还补充道："但不管你怎么看，这些合同都是长期的，而且我们明年的车手阵容已经百分之百满了。"
丰田目前参加世界耐力锦标赛（WEC），一台车由迈克·康威、尼克·德弗里斯和小林可梦伟驾驶，另一台车由塞巴斯蒂安·布埃米、布伦登·哈特利和平川亮驾驶。这家日本厂商刚刚在家乡富士赛道赢得胜利，在惊心动魄的尾声中，本地英雄平川亮完成了决定胜负的最后一段驾驶。
detailEn: Toyota denies 2027 WEC deal with Esteban Ocon
The Japanese manufacturer doesn't want to jeopardise the harmony within its driver lineups
Esteban Ocon’s Formula 1 options are gradually running out, and Toyota will not provide one in the WEC.

After Haas officially announced this week that it will end its partnership with the 30-year-old Frenchman at the conclusion of the 2026 season, media speculation has been rife over where Ocon’s career might take him next.
With Aston Martin having confirmed that it will continue with Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll, Cadillac effectively remains Ocon's last realistic option in Formula 1.

That is why he has also been linked with a possible switch to the World Endurance Championship – potentially with Toyota. But Toyota advisor Alexander Wurz has now made it clear to Motorsport.com sister publication Formel1.de’s YouTube channel: "There's nothing to these rumours."
Wurz said that Toyota generally plans "relatively far ahead" when it comes to Le Mans and its WEC programme, and that no changes to its current six-driver line-up are planned.

"Because when you put three alpha personalities in one car, it takes time for them to accept each other, to find the right set-up and the right way of working together, and to reach a point where they don't compete against each other internally but actually bring out the best in one another. That's a very important distinction," the Austrian explained.
#8 Toyota Gazoo Racing Toyota TR010: Sebastien Buemi, Brendon Hartley, Ryo Hirakawa
"That's one of Toyota's strengths: we have this team structure and this team culture, and you can't simply change that overnight.

"First of all, we have long-term contracts. And secondly, you can't just bring in another driver from the outside and slot him into the line-up. That would risk disrupting exactly the culture we've been building and nurturing since 2012. Maintaining that culture is one of my main responsibilities as an advisor and someone who works closely with the drivers.
He added: "But whichever way you look at it, the contracts are long-term and our line-up for next year is 100% full."

Toyota currently competes in the WEC with Mike Conway, Nyck de Vries and Kamui Kobayashi in one car, and Sebastien Buemi, Brendon Hartley and Ryo Hirakawa in the other. The Japanese manufacturer has just won its home race at Fuji, following a thrilling finish with local hero Hirakawa at the wheel for the decisive stint.

relatedItems.originalTitle: Honda secretly introduced second F1 ADUO upgrade in Madrid
relatedItems.summaryEn: Honda Racing Corporation president Koji Watanabe has revealed that Honda introduced its second ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) upgrade as early as the Spanish Grand Prix, focusing on the power unit's turbocharger.
detailZh: 本田秘密在马德里引入第二个F1 ADUO升级
本田赛车公司（HRC）透露，本田本赛季F1的第二个ADUO升级是新的涡轮增压器，早在西班牙大奖赛就已引入。
本田赛车公司社长渡边浩司透露，本田实际上早在F1西班牙大奖赛就引入了第二个额外开发与升级机会升级，重点针对动力单元的涡轮增压器。
阿斯顿·马丁和本田从赛季开始时表现挣扎，但在亨格罗林引入重大底盘升级后表现略有改善。在赞德沃特，车队还引入了搭载第一个ADUO升级的动力单元。
据测量，本田的内燃机（ICE）比红牛福特动力总成的引擎落后超过4%，后者被评为输出功率最高的引擎，这意味着本田获准在赛季中使用两个空气动力学升级配额令牌。
本田和HRC此前曾解释说，他们只会使用其中一次ADUO机会。“我们两次都用了，”渡边在接受Motorsport.com网站采访时透露，当时他被问到为什么本田决定只使用一次ADUO升级。
“我们在荷兰引入了第一次ADUO升级，然后在西班牙大奖赛上，我们把一套包含第二次升级的动力单元装到了斯特罗尔的车上。
“我们在荷兰引入的2号规格动力单元存在一些可驾驶性问题，所以我们在西班牙大奖赛上引入了一个改进版的涡轮增压器。”
事实上，国际汽联的动力单元部件使用清单显示，斯特罗尔的赛车在西班牙大奖赛时已经用上了本赛季的第五个涡轮增压器。费尔南多·阿隆索的赛车也在阿塞拜疆大奖赛装上了第五个涡轮增压器，而这看起来就是升级版本。
当被问及目标是否是解决涡轮迟滞问题时，渡边回答说：“是的。”他随后解释了分阶段引入升级部件的思路。
“如果我们能一次性把所有东西都引入当然更好，但首先在荷兰引入规格2（Spec 2）非常重要。与此同时，我们也在研究解决涡轮迟滞的对策，所以在西班牙引入了这部分。
“因此，应用最终被分成了两部分。”
不过渡边也表示，本田仍未完全发挥其动力单元的全部潜力。
本田此前为红牛供应引擎时，不被允许引入性能升级，但仍继续利用模拟来确定动力单元的运行极限，并逐年逐步提高这些极限。这就是本田所说的“可靠性研发”。
例如，红牛在2024年采用了极其窄小的侧箱，同时也缩小了用于引入冷却气流的开口尺寸。这也得益于提高动力单元的运行极限才得以实现。
“就ADUO而言，我们已经用完了本赛季的升级机会。从这里开始，我们将继续在不涉及硬件的方面下功夫，同时也进行面向未来发展的研发。”渡边说道。
我认为我们距离完全发挥这套动力单元的全部性能还很远。我相信它的竞争力仍有提升空间。
此前仍有一些地方存在动力不足，因此我们带着明确的目标数值开发了第二版规格。我们已经达成了这些目标，所以在赛季剩余的时间里，我们的重点将放在充分利用现有成果上，而不是继续开发硬件。
即便如此，我们仍要确保自己能够真正地进行竞争。
detailEn: Honda secretly introduced second F1 ADUO upgrade in Madrid
Honda's second ADUO upgrade of the F1 season was a new turbocharger, already introduced at the Spanish Grand Prix, HRC reveals

Honda Racing Corporation president Koji Watanabe has revealed that Honda actually introduced its second ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) upgrade as early as Formula 1’s Spanish Grand Prix, with the upgrade focused on the power unit's turbocharger.

Aston Martin and Honda struggled from the start of the season, but their performance slightly improved after a major chassis upgrade was introduced at the Hungaroring. In Zandvoort, the team also introduced a power unit fitted with the first ADUO upgrade.

Honda's ICE was measured to be more than 4% behind the Red Bull Ford Powertrains engine, which was rated as having the highest output, meaning Honda was granted permission to use two ADUO tokens during the season.

Honda and HRC had previously explained that they would use only one of those ADUO opportunities. “We used both of them,” Watanabe revealed to Motorsport.com when asked why Honda had decided to use only one ADUO upgrade.
“We introduced the first ADUO upgrade in the Netherlands, and then we put a PU incorporating the second update into Lance Stroll's car at the Spanish Grand Prix.
“The Spec 2 PU we introduced in the Netherlands had some drivability issues, so we introduced an improved turbo at the Spanish Grand Prix.”

Indeed, the FIA's list of PU component usage shows that Stroll's car was fitted with its fifth turbocharger of the season at the Spanish GP. Fernando Alonso's car was also fitted with his fifth turbo, which would appear to be the upgraded version, at the Azerbaijan GP.
Asked whether the objective was to address turbo lag, Watanabe replied: “Yes.” He subsequently explained the thinking behind the staggered introduction of the upgrades.

“It would have been better if we could have introduced everything at once, but it was important to introduce Spec 2 in the Netherlands first. We were also working on measures to address the turbo lag in parallel, so we introduced that in Spain.
“So the application ended up being split between the two.”
Watanabe also said, however, that Honda is still not extracting the full potential of its power unit.

When Honda was previously supplying Red Bull, it was not allowed to introduce performance upgrades, but it continued to use simulations to determine the operating limits of the PU and gradually raise those limits year after year. This was what Honda referred to as “reliability development”.

For example, Red Bull adopted extremely small sidepods in 2024, while also reducing the size of the openings used to draw in airflow for cooling. This was also made possible by raising the PU's operating limits.

“As far as ADUO is concerned, we have used up our opportunities for this season. From here, we will continue working on things that don't involve hardware, as well as developments that will lead into the future”, Watanabe said.
“I don't think we are anywhere near extracting the full performance of the PU. I believe there is still room to improve its competitiveness.

“There were still areas where we were lacking power, so we developed Spec 2 with target figures in mind. We have achieved those targets, so for the remainder of the season, our focus will be on making full use of what we have, rather than continuing to develop the hardware.
“Even so, we want to make sure we are able to fight properly.”

在赞德沃特，车队还引入了搭载第一个ADUO升级的动力单元。
渡边浩司是本田赛车公司的社长。
keyPointsEn: Aston Martin and Honda struggled from the start of the season, but performance slightly improved after a major chassis upgrade at the Hungaroring.
In Zandvoort, the team also introduced a power unit fitted with the first ADUO upgrade.
